text.en:
At the playground Ali watched many things move: a ball rolling straight, a merry-go-round, a swing and a clock's pendulum.
"Do all move in the same way?" he asked.
"No," said his teacher, "there are different types of motion."

An object is in motion when its position changes with time. Things move in different ways.
Rectilinear motion is along a straight line, such as a car on a straight road. Circular motion is along a circle, such as a stone tied to a string and whirled around.
Rotational motion is spinning about a fixed axis, such as a top, a fan or the Earth. Oscillatory motion is a to-and-fro movement about a fixed point, such as a swing or a pendulum.
Periodic motion repeats after equal intervals of time, such as a pendulum, the Earth going around the Sun, or the second hand of a clock.
A motion can be of more than one type. A wheel of a moving bicycle both rotates and moves along a straight line.
Something moves when its position changes with time.
A car on a straight road moves in a straight line. This is rectilinear motion.
A top spins about an axis. A swing goes to and fro. These are rotation and oscillation.
Motion that repeats after equal time is periodic, like a pendulum.

problem.en: What type of motion does a swing show?

text.en: A swing goes forward and backward again and again.

why.en: The movement is to and fro.

text.en: It moves about a fixed point.
So the swing shows oscillatory motion, which is also periodic.

prompt.en: Your friend says a spinning top has no motion because it stays at one place. How will you correct him?

requiredIdeas.en: It spins about a fixed axis, which is rotational motion.
Motion does not always mean moving from one place to another.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking motion must change the place.

points.en: Motion types: rectilinear, circular, rotational, oscillatory.
Periodic motion repeats after equal times.
One object can show more than one type of motion.
